entries.text: 1. **Rehearsal cannot reach completion through its normal controls.** At the last cue, the button changes to “Finish” while becoming disabled; the alternative finish action is hidden.
entries.source_excerpt: 1. **Rehearsal cannot reach completion through its normal controls.** At the last cue, the button changes to “Finish” while becoming disabled; the alternative finish action is hidden.

entries.text: 2. **The documented role boundary is not enforced consistently.** Viewers are described as read-only, yet the hold, timer, and speaker-ready mutation endpoints authorize the minimum `viewer` role.
entries.source_excerpt: 2. **The documented role boundary is not enforced consistently.** Viewers are described as read-only, yet the hold, timer, and speaker-ready mutation endpoints authorize the minimum `viewer` role.

entries.text: 3. **The forced temporary-password rule is page-only.** Proxy redirects force the set-password screen for pages but explicitly exempt every `/api/` path; shared API guards do not reject `must_change_password` sessions.
entries.source_excerpt: 3. **The forced temporary-password rule is page-only.** Proxy redirects force the set-password screen for pages but explicitly exempt every `/api/` path; shared API guards do not reject `must_change_password` sessions.

entries.text: 4. **External API control is exposed but structurally cannot obtain the controller lease.** Settings can create credentials, but every advertised control action reaches a locked live action and the API offers no claim...
entries.source_excerpt: 4. **External API control is exposed but structurally cannot obtain the controller lease.** Settings can create credentials, but every advertised control action reaches a locked live action and the API offers no claim-control action.

entries.text: 5. **Excel import is not one atomic operation.** Session upserts commit before the separate program-replacement RPC; a later failure leaves partial state.
entries.source_excerpt: 5. **Excel import is not one atomic operation.** Session upserts commit before the separate program-replacement RPC; a later failure leaves partial state.

entries.text: 6. **Production has multiple live origins.** `app.kramflow.me` serves the product instead of redirecting to `www`; local auth cookies are host-scoped. The resulting login/session split is a strong risk, though cross-h...
entries.source_excerpt: 6. **Production has multiple live origins.** `app.kramflow.me` serves the product instead of redirecting to `www`; local auth cookies are host-scoped. The resulting login/session split is a strong risk, though cross-host authentication was not destructively tested.

entries.text: 7. **Required trust/operations foundations are incomplete.** Privacy and terms pages are absent, and no production error-monitoring integration was found—material for an account-based live-event system.
entries.source_excerpt: 7. **Required trust/operations foundations are incomplete.** Privacy and terms pages are absent, and no production error-monitoring integration was found—material for an account-based live-event system.

entries.text: 8. **Security and email release gates need closure.** No CSP is deployed. Email DNS has DKIM and monitoring-only DMARC, but no root SPF record was returned and delivered-message alignment was unavailable.

## P1 — Rehearsal Finish is disabled

**Wrong:** At the final cue, the primary control reads **Finish** but is disabled. The alternate finish action is hidden.

**Why it matters:** The core rehearsal cannot complete and has no trustworthy ending—the highest-impact point in the workflow.

**Likely root cause:** One condition is used for both “already finished” and “currently at the final cue”: `disabled={isFinished || currentOrder >= max}`. The state transition expects an order beyond `max`, but no control can produce it.

**Fix:** Enable Finish when `currentOrder === max`; call a dedicated completion action. Render a concise completion summary. Preserve the current architectural guarantee that rehearsal never writes live state.

entries.text: P1 — Excel import does not lead clearly to a runnable session. Wrong: import refreshes session data but does not set the live active session; Console can show 'Select a session to get started' with no inline choice/action. Why it matters: a successful onboarding action appears to strand the operator immediately before the product's main job. Root cause supported by source: imported sessions and live active session are separate state; the server also upserts sessions before a separate replacement RPC, so the operation is not fully atomic, and derives affected IDs from programs, omitting empty imported sessions. Fix: move session upsert and affected-session program replacement into one transaction; derive affected IDs from parsed sessions and return generic client errors; on success, identify the imported/default session and offer 'Open Console with [session]'; validate on activation that the session belongs to the event; require an explicit choice when multiple sessions exist. Acceptance criteria (one unbulleted paragraph in the source — the exact text the extractor's list/table pass cannot see): New event -> valid XLSX -> confirmation -> session selection -> Console -> Start works without a hidden header action. ## P1 — Excel import does not lead clearly to a runnable session

**Wrong:** Import refreshes session data but does not set the live active session. Console can show “Select a session to get started” without an inline choice/action.

**Why it matters:** A successful onboarding action appears to strand the operator immediately before the product’s main job.

**Root cause supported by source:** imported sessions and live active session are separate state. The cue sheet defaults its local view to the first session, while live state remains empty. The server also upserts sessions before a separate replacement RPC, so the operation is not fully atomic; it derives affected IDs from programs, omitting empty imported sessions.

**Fix:** Move session upsert and affected-session program replacement into one transaction. Derive affected IDs from parsed sessions and return generic client errors. On success, identify the imported/default session, show it in the success state, and offer **Open Console with [session]**. On activation, validate that the session belongs to the event. If multiple sessions exist, require an explicit choice rather than guessing.

**Acceptance criteria:** New event → valid XLSX → confirmation → session selection → Console → Start works without a hidden header action. Refresh preserves a coherent choice. Invalid/empty/duplicate/oversized files show actionable errors and do not partially mutate data.

## P1 — Viewer/editor role promises are bypassed by stage-state APIs

**Wrong:** KramFlow says viewers are read-only and only owners run the live show. The shared `verifySessionAccess` guard accepts `viewer`, and the hold, timer, and speaker-ready PATCH routes use it before service-role writes.

**Why it matters:** A viewer can bypass disabled UI and change operational state through direct authenticated requests. Hold and timer changes can affect live displays.

**Fix:** Write the intended permission matrix first. Require owner for live/display mutations unless a specifically named backstage role is introduced. Keep read-only display-token behavior separate. Do not rely on hidden/disabled controls.

**Acceptance criteria:** Direct endpoint tests prove viewer and editor receive 403 for every owner-only mutation; owner succeeds; unrelated and anonymous users fail generically; UI text matches server truth.

## P1 — Forced password replacement is only a page redirect

**Wrong:** invited users with `must_change_password=true` are forced to `/set-password` for pages, but proxy exempts `/api/` and shared API guards ignore the flag.

**Why it matters:** Anyone holding the temporary emailed password can create a session and use authenticated APIs without completing the promised credential replacement.

**Fix:** Add the flag check to shared user/event API authorization. Narrowly allow auth login/logout/set-password and endpoints whose authorization is intentionally a display/integration token rather than a user session.

**Acceptance criteria:** A flagged user can log in, set a password, or log out—and nothing else. Event reads, invitation acceptance, cue edits, exports, live actions, and stage-state writes all fail until the flag is cleared.

entries.text: P1 — External API control cannot obtain the controller lease. Wrong: Settings creates credentials and documents control actions, but the adapter forwards a synthetic integration client ID to owner-locked actions without exposing claim/renew/release/takeover, so normal calls hit 423 Locked. Why it matters: a visible integration feature promises control that cannot work reliably. Fix: safest pre-launch choice is to disable credential creation and label the feature Coming Soon; to ship it, define lease acquisition, renewal, expiry, takeover, idempotency, replay/rate limits, and human-operator precedence; never bypass the existing lease silently. Acceptance criteria: a documented integration can acquire and renew control, perform each allowed action, release/expire safely, and receive deterministic 401/403/409/423 behavior; human takeover and audit logs are verified under concurrency.

**Why it matters:** A visible integration feature promises control that cannot work reliably, exactly the concern behind marking it Coming Soon.

**Fix:** Safest pre-launch choice: disable credential creation and label the control feature Coming Soon. To ship it, define lease acquisition, renewal, expiry, takeover, idempotency, replay/rate limits, and human-operator precedence; never bypass the existing lease silently.
